# Requirements Document: A-la-carte offer items

## Introduction

An a-la-carte offer item is an optional ancillary with a unit price and the
passengers and segments it may be bought for.  It holds no flight.  The add bag
worked example buys one at quantity 1 for one passenger over two journeys and
gets two order items, one per journey, each at the unit price.  The model
follows the worked example: one order item for each passenger and segment
chosen, each at the unit price times the quantity.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Ancillaries/AlaCarte.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-air/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Ancillaries/AlaCarte.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-606

**User Story:** As a seller, I want an extra bag priced the same way every time, so that I can quote the customer the right amount before they pay.

**Rule:** WHEN a seller chooses an a-la-carte offer item for passengers and segments it lists as eligible THE SYSTEM SHALL create one order item for each passenger and segment chosen, at the unit price times the quantity. (Lean: `chooseAlaCarte`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. IF an a-la-carte choice names a passenger or a segment that the offer item does not list as eligible THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it.
   - ONE-606.1, proven: proven theorem `alacarte_refuses_ineligible`; example `bagForIneligiblePassenger`
2. WHEN an a-la-carte choice is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL create one order item for each passenger and segment chosen, each holding one service for that passenger on that segment.
   - ONE-606.2, proven: proven theorem `alacarte_item_per_passenger_segment`; example `bagOverTwoJourneys`
3. WHEN an a-la-carte choice is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL price each order item at the unit price times the quantity.
   - ONE-606.3, proven: proven theorem `alacarte_item_price`; example `bagOverTwoJourneys`
4. WHEN an a-la-carte choice is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL make the total price of its order items the unit price times the quantity times the number of passengers and segments chosen.
   - ONE-606.4, proven: proven theorem `alacarte_total`; example `bagOverTwoJourneys`
5. WHEN an a-la-carte offer item is ordered THE SYSTEM SHALL create exactly one order item from it.
   - ONE-606.5, open: open theorem `alacarte_one_item`; counterexample `bagOverTwoJourneys`

#### Open question on ONE-606.5

> An a-la-carte offer item becomes exactly one order item, as every offer
> item does when an offer is accepted.
>
> Open question for the business.  The add bag worked example orders a 50.00 bag
> at quantity 1 for one passenger over two journeys and gets two order items of
> 50.00, so one offer item becomes two order items and the bag costs 100.00.
> The example `bagOverTwoJourneys` shows it.  Does one offer item become one
> order item, as the order structure says, or one per passenger and segment, as
> the worked example shows?  And what is the unit of the unit price: a passenger
> on a segment, a journey, or the order?
